olivia (Support): Hey team, Acme just pinged — they got charged twice for a single webhook-triggered action. They say our model invoked the payment tool twice. Can we triage?

acct-customer-ops (Acme Inc.): Confirmed — one user action led to two identical charges ~30s apart. We have transaction IDs: txn_20260301_01 and txn_20260301_02. Only meant to be one.

maya (SRE): Thanks. Can you paste the request ids / X-Redwood-Request-ID from your app logs? We need mapping to our runtime traces.

acct-customer-ops (Acme Inc.): App logs show X-Redwood-Request-ID: r-9f8c7b6a and invocation_id: inv-44f2. Also include our original client-side idempotency key idemp-abc-123.

olivia (Support): Pasting the runtime logs we pulled:```
[2026-03-01T15:03:12Z] r-9f8c7b6a START -> model: gpt-4x, tool_policy: enable-tools
[2026-03-01T15:03:12Z] inv-44f2 -> tool_call: charge_customer args={"amount":100,"user_id":"u-33"}
[2026-03-01T15:03:12Z] inv-44f2 -> upstream: POST https://payments.partner/charge  -> 200 OK
[2026-03-01T15:03:12Z] inv-44f2 -> exec status: completed
[2026-03-01T15:03:42Z] r-9f8c7b6a REPLAY -> token refresh path hit, auth reinit
[2026-03-01T15:03:42Z] r-9f8c7b6a -> model responded with fallback instruction: "caller should call /charge now"
[2026-03-01T15:03:42Z] inv-44f2-replay -> exec status: completed (external webhook)```

olivia (Support): Looks like first execution succeeded and then a replay/fallback caused a second external webhook firing ~30s later.

siva (Runtime Eng): Important detail — the first call is a tool_call (structured function call) that our runtime executes as a webhook plugin. The second path appears to be a fallback from the model to plain-text instruction which our old fallback runner still executes as a safety-run.

maya (SRE): Do we have the model response bodies? Need to confirm whether the second response had "function_call" or plain text.

olivia (Support): I grabbed both gziped responses from logs. Snippet:```
=== response @ 15:03:12 ===
{"choices": [{"message": {"role":"assistant","content":null,"function_call":{"name":"charge_customer","arguments":"{\"amount\":100,\"user_id\":\"u-33\"}"}}]} }
=== response @ 15:03:42 ===
{"choices": [{"message": {"role":"assistant","content":"Please POST to https://payments.partner/charge with payload {user_id: 'u-33', amount: 100}","function_call":null}}]}
```

siva (Runtime Eng): That matches: first is function_call, second is plain-text fallback. Our fallback worker (legacy) is configured to try to execute any actionable instruction it sees. That explains duplicate exec.

ton y (Oncall): @siva what triggered the fallback? We saw a token refresh event in the trace before the second response. Could the model have re-evaluated the prompt mid-flight and produced a fallback?

siva (Runtime Eng): Likely. We recently rolled a change to how we handle auth refresh during long-running requests: if mid-request auth refresh happens, we re-synthesize the prompt and re-call the model to finish. That can generate a non-tool alternative if the model chooses. Bug is that during re-call we still allow the legacy fallback executor to run.

maya (SRE): Action items: 1) stop legacy fallback executor from invoking webhooks for any response that matches a prior invocation id. 2) Verify runtime dedup by invocation_id or X-Redwood-Request-ID. 3) Refund the duplicate charge.

billing-joe: I'll prepare refund for txn_20260301_02 once we confirm it's duplicate. Please mark it confirmed so I can run the reverse-charge flow.

olivia (Support): Repro steps from dev copy:```
1) Use SDK vX.Y with idempotency-key=idemp-abc-123
2) Send prompt that calls `charge_customer` via tool call
3) During the model run, trigger an auth refresh (we reproduced by dropping the runtime token for ~1s)
4) Observe that runtime re-invokes model; model returns plain text instruction; legacy fallback runner executes it -> duplicate external POST
```

siva (Runtime Eng): Quick mitigation: hotfix to disable legacy fallback executor for any request where `invocation_id` has recorded a `tool_call` completed event. Deploying patch now to turn on a guard: `if tool_call_completed(invocation_id) => skip fallback-exec`

redwood-deploy-bot: Deploy started: patch/runtime/fallback-guard -> canary on hosts runtime-03..05

redwood-deploy-bot: Deploy success: canary passed, rollout to 80%

maya (SRE): Good. Next: we should add server-side dedup using a charge idempotency header when invoking partner API: set `X-Idempotency-Key: inv-44f2` so partner ignores replay. Siva could you add that to webhook plugin?

siva (Runtime Eng): Yep. Also adding a runtime invariant: never auto-exec plain-text instructions that duplicate a function_call we already executed in same invocation. I'll open PR and backport to the 6.4.x runtime.

olivia (Support): I'll tell Acme we're treating txn_20260301_02 as duplicate and we'll process refund. ETA: billing-joe, can you confirm when refund completes?

billing-joe: Preparing refund now. Should be done in ~30m, I'll update this thread with confirmation and refund id.

olivia (Support): Final follow-ups: - Siva/Maya file postmortem (root cause: auth-refresh -> re-call -> fallback-exec race) - Ensure SDK change: don't trigger automatic client retries when server indicates a function_call already executed (we should surface a 2xx+body rather than retry).

acct-customer-ops (Acme Inc.): Thanks all — appreciate quick fix. Please share postmortem and the refund id.

olivia (Support): Will do. Marking resolved once billing-joe posts refund id. :white_check_mark:
